# Port Checklist: Bring the reference game's features, correctly and fast

**Purpose**: the quality of the requirements that govern the port (US4) and its loop: each feature's sheet, its design in this
game's architecture, its checks and photos in seconds, nothing copied from the reference, the budgets
**Created**: 2026-11-13
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Is "a feature" defined precisely enough that an area's unpaired inventory rows can be grouped into features the same way twice? [Clarity, Spec §Key Entities, Tasks T007]
- [ ] CHK002 Are the sections a comparison sheet must hold specified, including the reference's faults and the norm its rule is judged against? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008, §FR-021, contracts/comparison-sheet.md]
- [ ] CHK003 Is it specified what makes an unpaired row "justified" (a fault, a lab-only tool, a superseded design) and who records why? [Completeness, Spec §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK004 Are the architecture rules a ported feature must follow (CityState, commands, simulation, render read-only, DataTables, one owner, budgets) stated in the spec or referenced to the constitution? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009, Constitution VIII]
- [ ] CHK005 Is the list of the reference's faults that must never be brought referenced from the requirements (whole-map work, per-frame work on unchanged inputs, allocation in hot loops, quadratic proximity, heavy geometry)? [Completeness, Spec §US4, Constitution VI]
- [ ] CHK006 Are the area order and the rule for choosing it (the inventory's player-facing gaps) documented with the counts it was decided on? [Completeness, Tasks Phase 3]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK007 Is "checked in seconds" quantified (each check under 60 s, an item's verdict under 60 s)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010, §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK008 Is "photos aimed at what it changed" specified with the views required (distances, bearings, elevations, day and night where light is involved)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010, §FR-013, Constitution X]
- [ ] CHK009 Is "paired" defined by evidence the inventory can show after a feature is built, not by a claim? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007, §SC-010]
- [ ] CHK010 Is "nothing copied" made measurable (the copy scan's result of zero over the feature's files, the text keys included)? [Measurability, Spec §FR-009, §FR-015, §SC-006]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK011 Do the priority of US4 (P1, first) in the spec, the plan's phases and the tasks' order agree? [Consistency, Spec §US4, Plan §Phases, Tasks]
- [ ] CHK012 Do the per-item commit rule (SC-007) and the area tasks (two tasks per area, many features each) agree on what one commit holds? [Consistency, Spec §SC-007, Tasks T007-T027]
- [ ] CHK013 Are the camera's requirements (FR-001 to FR-005) consistent with its place as the port's last area? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001, Tasks T026-T027]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK014 Does each area task's "Done when" name a check that can be run and read (the unpaired list, the scenes, the photos, the copy scan)? [Measurability, Tasks T007-T027]
- [ ] CHK015 Is a budget criterion stated per ported feature (no budget the previous build kept broken), and when it is measured? [Measurability, Spec §FR-023, §SC-012]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK016 Are requirements defined for a reference feature that exists here under a different text or design (paired by behaviour, not by text)? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK017 Are requirements defined for a reference feature whose behaviour is itself a fault (its behaviour brought, its cost not)? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK018 Are requirements defined for a feature that changes the city's digest or the save format (the reference written again with its cause; old saves)? [Coverage, Gap]
- [ ] CHK019 Are requirements defined for a feature the tracer cannot follow (a gap it reports: read by hand, the tracer's failure registered)? [Coverage, Gap]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK020 Are the median and floor profiles' budgets referenced with their numbers for every ported system? [Clarity, Spec §FR-023, doc/specification.md]
- [ ] CHK021 Are memory requirements stated for ported state (memory never growing with the area explored, records kept as parameters)? [Coverage, Constitution VI]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK022 Is the assumption that the reference stays readable on this machine stated with what happens when it is not? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions, §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK023 Are the tools the loop depends on (inventory, tracer, look plans with setViewNear, the block close's method check) listed as prerequisites of the first area? [Dependency, Tasks Phase 2]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
